methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $58M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
Verdant Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Gabe Sibley and Curtis Garner that has raised $58M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B Series B, Dexterity at $1.6B Series B, and Walden Robotics at $1.1B Seed), alongside 1 public comparable and a broader private universe of 8 firms including Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression modeling applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the $58M raised proxy, yielding $116M. Peer-median analysis across the 3 comparable companies produces a $1.6B midpoint valuation, with a range of $1.1B to $1.8B. These two methods generate a wide implied range reflecting the different approaches: early-stage cash-multiple sizing versus sector comparables.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $99M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $883M. The substantial width reflects structural uncertainty inherent in valuing pre-revenue or early-stage robotics ventures: stage-progression methods anchor to realized capital but ignore peer-market signals, while peer-median methods may not reflect Verdant's specific technology, market opportunity, or burn profile. Resolution of this range would benefit from visibility on Verdant's revenue traction, unit economics, and technical differentiation relative to the named peer set.
